utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning everybody. The case be called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Nicholas Koumjian with Morten Bergsmo and case manager Ruth Karper for the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic this morning accompanied by the young Mr. Danilo Cirkovic our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Welcome aboard. The Chamber has revisited the problem of what is the best way to protect the witness and the idea was whether or not it is better to proceed in closed session, instead of jumping in and out. We should have thought about this yesterday, but we were not aware about this beforehand. I think it is such a situation it is better to do the entire issue in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BERGSMO
utterances.text: The Prosecution would concur with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Defence concur, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we proceed in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 1 (redacted) 2 (redacted) 3 (redacted) 4 (redacted) 5 (redacted) 6 (redacted) 7 (redacted) 8 (redacted) 9 (redacted) 10 (redacted) 11 (redacted) 12 (redacted) 13 (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We resume in open session and turn immediately to the motion of the Office of the Prosecutor on 92 bis witnesses. And I don't think it's necessary that the OTP once again comments why or why not. We know it from the entire bundle of documents. But before we decide, we indeed want to have the observations from the side of the Defence, taking into account that we should call the witnesses only by number, not by name, because we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. Without belabouring the point and addressing obviously what we think is the inherent right for an accused to have the right of faith and to cross-examine the witnesses brought before him, we believe that from the list that was provided to us of the proposed 92 bis witnesses, we would have no objection to the following 65 ter numbered witnesses. However, before I list those out, I would like, just for the record, to make the commentary, we were given an exhaustive amount of material, naturally. Some of the material we have slight objections to because the cross-examination of various witnesses were not provided. I think it may have just been our perhaps our oversight or the oversight, but I am sure they would want to provide the complete transcript of those witnesses particularly where we do not have an objection to them. Specifically I'm referencing Witness 59, but we could address that at a later time. Also, to the extent that any of these documents or witnesses, documents meaning their statements, are brought forth, and I recognise, obviously respectfully, the position of the Court, reading 92 bis, It’s essentially in my view, prohibited to allow these statements to come in if they go towards the acts or conduct of the accused. Given that, if, for some instance, either the Office of the Prosecution or the Defence allows a statement to go in, and it does address that issue, we would obviously take an exception to that and ask to be heard on that limited basis. We think from our review that should not come up, but, again in an attempt to preserve the rights of the accused, we have to mention that as a provision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This should be quite clear from the outset, that every kind of ruling as regards this matter is, of course, and by nature only a provisional one. There may be the one or other witness bringing us to other conclusions and pointing out the need to hear witness, be it ex officio or be it on the request of the one or the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may proceed, the following witnesses, we would not have an objection, keeping in mind the comments that we've made. And thank you, judge, for those. They are 65 ter number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Number 15, Number 19, Number 20, Number 25, Number 32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wait a minute. 25, you said. And then?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Number 32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I can't find --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 2 of the witness list proposed by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You're quite sure it's not 38?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think there's a confusion there that's due to a motion that's pending before the president. So that's all I can say in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So you want to make reference to the 65 ter Number 38. Is this right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No. Counsel stated the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For a moment, we go in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And finally, Number 78 on our list obviously states that it's going to be a 92 bis, but I think that's behind us now because Dr. Donia has already testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, of course, we have to ask the Office of the Prosecutor, and may we have the additional appearance, please, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and case manager Ruth Karper. We'll check on the issue of the transcript, but I believe it's page 3219 of the transcript, and the cross-examination was apparently quite short. You may check your copy to see if maybe you missed it. But as for the rest of these, Your Honour, it's our position that in the interests of the brevity of the trial and the efficiency of the trial, most of these witnesses we could go through them one by one are testifying to matters that other witnesses are coming in and testifying to live. I have a particular comment about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we probably take the opportunity, go through the rest of the -- the remaining witnesses. Immediately, I can say that the Judges came to the conclusion that it's indispensable to hear witness Number 1 live. Number 2 is now accepted by all the parties under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Your Honour is referring to Number 6 via 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's the 6 of the 65 ter number, yeah, indeed. Then there are no specific contributions on this witness, protected witness 7, the Judges came to the conclusion that this is to be regarded as admitted under 92 bis. As regards Number 15 of the 65 ter list, I take it that it's accepted by the parties and the Judges that this goes under 92 bis. As regards Number 19, the same is true as it was just said with respect to Witness 15. May we for a moment go into private session as regards Witness 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As regards the objected number 38, the question from the side of the Judges is, wouldn't it be possible for the Office of the Prosecutor to withdraw the entire witness and the statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the exercises that we would do at the end of Your Honours' ruling is to decide on each of the witnesses the Court does not accept the 92 bis, whether or not it is worth the time that would be involved and other considerations to bring that witness. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. This particular witness -- if I could just have one moment. One of the reasons that we chose to ask to 92 bis this witness is because it's a corroborative witness of Witness 28. So if Your Honours rule that it's necessary for this witness to become live, we may decide that we have enough evidence with Witness 28 not to proceed. Witness 28 was -- has already testified -- excuse me. I'm sorry. It's pending, will testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So then for today, and I say once again, for today, Witness 38 will be accepted under 92 bis, if there is no other ruling in the future. Witness 44, the request from the side of the Judges is, once again, is it really necessary to include this witness and the statement? We're not able to identify specific important points related to the indictment before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, just one thing that stands out for me, looking at the 65 ter summary of this witness is the witness's ethnicity which is -- we don't have many witnesses of that ethnicity in the case. But we -- again, I'd rather reserve that decision, one, to see how it goes with the other witnesses. It's very possible that witnesses will drop out that we're anticipating will be here. We've already had some problems with that. So I don't want to drop these from our list and then have to reapply to add them as witnesses. If the Court feels it is necessary for the witness to come live, we'll evaluate whether it's necessary to include them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's not a question of whether they come live, it's only a question of whether to discuss this question under 92 bis. We didn't see any acceptance by the Defence, if I see it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps we can get some indication of why the -- what the cross-examination could -- the Defence could hope to achieve through that for this particular witness. If the Court rules they have to come for cross-examination, we will make them available for cross-examination or we'll decide to withdraw the witness, depending upon how the -- how we evaluate the total case at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if my learned friend was -- or perhaps I wasn't following you. It's not just necessarily a question of whereby the cross-examination will go as it relates to the items in the indictment, what we hope to -- or what I thought we were going to hopefully accomplish with this is to for lack of a better term weed out witnesses that are cumulative on nonessential paragraphs or witnesses that perhaps are unnecessary for any element or aspect of the indictment. To advise the Court and the OTP of what our cross-examination would be of this witness may take a little time. It may also put us at slightly a disadvantage that we don't necessarily want to share at this point. I don't think the Rule 92 bis asks for that from the Defence, but certainly if we can point to certain areas where we feel the acts or conduct are called in question as, by way of example, the witness number 1 was quite on its face obvious. This witness, in particular, we still can't figure out why the Prosecutor wants to call him. So our cross would be based on what the purpose is behind calling this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps I could help a little bit on that, thanks to the help of my colleague, Ms. Sutherland, who has a better knowledge of this witness. Your Honour, if you look at the -- I don't know if Your Honour and counsel have the 65 ter summary for this witness in front of them, but the summary includes all of the statement -- excuse me, I guess I'm reading from a different summary which is more detailed. But the statement of this witness goes beyond the period of time of this indictment. We would be willing and that's in the 65 ter summary, the third paragraph. We would be willing to take that out because it's beyond the period of the indictment. The reason this witness was selected was because of the ethnicity. Most of our witnesses are Muslims, and we wanted to show that this was a policy that applied to Croats also.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thus far, I don't believe in any of the questioning by the Defence did, when the witnesses stated whom were present at the various camps, did we ever cross them on the veracity of them having an understanding that there may have been some or a few or however they may have categorized the ethnicity of the Croatians. I don't know that -- we're not going to cross-examine her on whether she is truly of a certain ethnic background. That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we try to proceed under Rule 92 bis as regards Witness 44, and we would ask the Office of the Prosecutor or the Defence, if necessary, to come with other contributions, and, of course, as I indicated already in the beginning, the Chamber is always open for new views. Until now, 92 bis. The same is true with 49, accepted by the parties and by the Judges under Rule 92 bis. As regards 51, until now we did not have heard any special objections regarding this witness. And therefore, until further order, this witness statement is also admitted under 92 bis. The same is true for Witness 52. With Witness 53, we once again have a problem whether or not it would be better to withdraw this witness at all. There are statements about events in 1993, beyond the time in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, but if I could just point out to Your Honour what it talks about, this particular witness, is obviously a very organised effort to hide crimes that occurred. And this occurred -- my understanding is during the time that Dr. Stakic was still in power. This would be evidence of an attempt to hide a crime, and we think it's very, very relevant to the indictment. Large equipment was used, and explosives, and that's why we believe it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So having heard this, this Witness 53 goes, until further order, under 92 bis. And of course, it's for the Defence to demonstrate the special relevance and necessity of cross-examination. The same is true with Witness 54. Witness 59, here, the, Judges evidently in line with the Defence, want to hear this witness live. 59. Witness 85 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could I just comment on this. We didn't rather anticipate that ruling. This witness we're trying to schedule for June the 26th, if that is convenient for the Court and counsel, because the witness will also be testifying on the ARK case at approximately the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then Witness 85, it was accepted by the Judges and also the parties. And therefore, this witness goes under 92 bis. And once again, notwithstanding other objections in the future by the Defence, also Witness 86 goes under 92 bis. I just learned that -- let's go just for a minute to be on the safe side in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And there is just one document the registry may correct me if I am wrong, to be admitted into evidence, or even two. One was the document provided today by the Defence, D3. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But may it be called, please, the draft statute, to be quite correct and on the safe side here. And then finally, the receipt, if anybody could help me about the number --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: S12, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. S12. It was still objected. What is your position, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if you recall we did have an objection to this document. In comparing it to other receipts that were received from detainees at the Trnopolje camp, we noticed that other receipts do not have the added language. If the Court recalls, under the name of Pero Curguz, under his signature namely. It is difficult for us 3 to pass judgement whether that was particularly written by the individual on the right or the individual on the left. The witness certainly didn't testify that it was written by either. He did confirm the signature of those two. But we have by way of an example another receipt, "Potvrda", that I believe was given to us -- and I make this representation on the representation made to me -- by the Office of the Prosecutor. So we have a similar receipt for another detainee which doesn't have that information. It's a very important document from the Defence standpoint. And also, from an evidentiary standpoint. And I'm sure that the Court would want to protect that issue as well. So we must continue to insist on objecting to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Honestly, I don't understand you. It should be your point that this should be admitted into evidence that you can demonstrate as you want another document opposed to this. But please understand, under our rules, especially the guidelines on authenticity, this document is admitted into evidence under 12B. There were three objections, and...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It was on S3 through S6 -- S4 to S6. They were admitted -- offered the 18th of April, but the Defence reserved the right to object to the translation. Any comments from the Defence on this? S4 to S6, 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We don't believe that we've seen the translation of those, Your Honour. So we're not prepared to address that issue with the Court at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We come back to this on Monday in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think there's a little confusion, because I think those were marked 4A, 4B, the translations provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the registry show the documents to the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just a general comment, these are official translations, so I'm not sure that an objection to the translation, that we have to review it, is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have to decide this nevertheless when it's still open.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: True, our only comment was we did not at that time have the translation. But we do now obviously. We'll look at it. And as long as we have the translation we'll accept the translators' version of it. If something comes up that we think is perhaps obvious, we'll bring it to the Court attention when appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for the record and for the Registry, those documents are admitted into evidence as S4 to S6 A and B relatively. I don't want to go too much into other details today. I think we should come back to the question of the additional witness, and we have still a motion on this. But this can't be addressed today. What is the number of the witness we have to expect on Monday, 14.15?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 37 will be the next witness. To be followed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. by -- 37 is the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be followed by? Number 40 is no longer relevant? Because this was still on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. It's still relevant. There was a necessity to move that witness's arrival back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So it will be 37 next week, 26, and we have scheduled witness Number 9, although I think that's a little optimistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We'll try our best. And I think now the weekend is really well deserved. I thank the parties for cooperation. And see us on Monday, 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 4.41 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of May, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
